items.title: Flatness and formal smoothness of a local map versus regularity of its special fibre
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition proves the equivalence of three conditions on a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings: flatness together with geometric regularity of the special fibre, flatness together with formal smoothness of the fibre in the maximal-adic topology, and formal smoothness of the local map itself. One equivalence is quoted from the regular-fibre theorem and one implication follows from flatness of formally smooth maps plus base change, so the substance is the remaining implication: the author first replaces the rings by their completions, then chooses the standard diagram of a power series ring over a Cohen ring mapping to the target, cuts the target down by a regular sequence so that the special fibres become equal, and finishes with the lifting argument of the regular-fibre theorem in which a derivation into a square-zero ideal is adjusted by a map on differentials. The proof is a long, self-contained chain of reductions and is fully displayed.
